Consider the following statements about 'Suspension':
I. Suspension is not a penalty.
II. An employee under suspension must mark attendance in the school daily.
III. Subsistence allowance can be increased or decreased after the first three months of suspension based on the delay in inquiry.

questions.explanation_english: Statements I and III are correct. Suspension is generally an interim measure pending inquiry rather than a final penalty. questions.question_english: A private recognized unaided school faces a severe financial deficit and fails to pay teachers their salaries for three months. The teachers file a petition. The management claims inability to pay due to non-collection of fees. What is the legal stance under DSEA 1973?
options_english: Management is fully absolved of statutory liability if fees remain uncollected.
Salary payment under Section 10 is mandatory; financial incapacity is no defense.
Teachers are statutorily required to wait until the school recovers pending fees.
The DoE is legally required to disburse pending salaries in unaided school cases.
questions.explanation_english: Salary payment under Section 10 is mandatory; financial incapacity is no defense. Section 10 of the Delhi School Education Act, 1973 creates a mandatory statutory obligation for private school management to pay employees salaries at par with government staff. Financial deficit or fee non-collection offers no legal defense, and management remains bound to disburse complete statutory salaries and allowances.
